"The Box" is a song by American rapper Roddy Ricch, originally released on December 6, 2019 as the second track from his debut studio album Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial, before released as the fourth single on January 11, 2020. Prior to the song being released as a single, it became Roddy Ricch's highest-charting song worldwide, spending eleven weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, as well as topping the charts in Canada, New Zealand, Hungary, and peaking at number two in both the UK and Ireland. The song received critical acclaim, with praise for Ricch's vocal delivery. Its popularity on social media apps is credited to Ricch's iconic "eee err" ad-lib. A music video was released on February 28, 2020, directed by Ricch.

In the US, "The Box" was the biggest song of the final half of 2019, selling 4.7 million equivalent units as of July 2, 2020. Apple Music named it Song of the Year. It received three nominations at the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards: Best Rap Song, Best Melodic Rap Performance, and Song of the Year. It was Billboard magazine's number-one rap song of 2020, taking the top spot it's Year-End Hot Rap Songs of 2020. It also took the number-two spot on the Billboard Year-End Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs of 2020, being held from the top spot by The Weeknd's "Blinding Lights."

sections.heading: Background and composition
sections.wikitext:
"The Box" was the last song Ricch made for ''[[Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial]]''.<ref name="GQ">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gq.com/story/roddy-ricch-the-box-interview-2020|title=Chart-Topping Rapper Roddy Ricch Won't Let Superstardom Change Him|last=Schube|first=Will|date=January 24, 2020|website=[[GQ]]|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> It was recorded in roughly 15 minutes<ref name="Studio Sessions" /> in the early morning hours in New York after Ricch had been recording all night.<ref name="GQ" /> The song begins with a "triumphant introduction that amounts to an orchestral swell", which many listeners attributed to as a sample of the intro on "[[Love Sex Magic]]" by [[Ciara]].<ref name="30Roc">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/30-roc-interview-roddy-ricch-the-box-sample-8548888/|title=30 Roc on Producing the Beat to Roddy Ricch's No. 1 Hit 'The Box' and Those Opening Strings: 'It Is Not a Sample'|last=LeDonne|first=Rob|date=January 24, 2020|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|language=en|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> However, the song's producer, [[30 Roc]], has insisted that though similar, the "swell" is not a sample of "Love Sex Magic", explaining: "It is not a sample. It's really a VST [plug-in] using Omnisphere [production software]."<ref name="30Roc" /> Ricch said he decided to place "The Box" as track two on the album, because "it just bangs [and] the [[Roland TR-808|808s]] hit so hard".<ref name="Making The Box">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/roddy-ricch-the-box-interview/|title=Roddy Ricch Interview: Making The Box and His Chart-Topping Success|last=Lamarre|first=Carl|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=January 14, 2020|access-date=March 25, 2020}}</ref>

The song's intro contains a "squeaky sound", known as the "eee err" sound, which is also heard throughout the rest of the song. According to [[Atlantic Records]] [[Artists and repertoire|A&R]] Keefa Black, after the song was finished, Ricch said "Wait let me add something", and came up with the sound himself.<ref>{{Cite tweet|url=https://twitter.com/KEEFABLACK/status/1214275540175114242|title=we made The Box at 6am in NYC after being up all night...|last=Black|first=Keefa|date=January 6, 2020|user=KEEFABLACK|accessdate=February 16, 2020|number=1214275540175114242}}</ref> Speaking on where the inspiration for the sound came from, he said "I seen [[Michael Jackson]] do it...That's what made me want to do it. Cause he was in the studio one time and he was talking about some song that he made but he started [[beatboxing]] and he said he put that in the beat".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/268586-roddy-ricch-the-box-sound-effects-inspired-by-michael-jackson-news|title=Roddy Ricch "The Box" Sound Effects Inspired By Michael Jackson|website=HotNewHipHop|last=A.|first=Aron|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}}</ref> The squeaky sound has inspired many memes online.<ref name="OCC">{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/who-is-roddy-ricch-the-rapper-taking-over-the-world-with-tik-tok-viral-song-the-box__28456/|title=Who is Roddy Ricch? The rapper taking over with viral hit The Box|date=January 24, 2020|website=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> [[Musicologist#Education and careers|Musicologist]] and [[Northeastern University]]  professor of music Andrew Mall said the "eee err" sound is not exactly the most interesting component of the song's beat, instead pointing out Ricch's skill as a songwriter: "I'm really taken by the atmospheric [[Synthesizer|synths]] that underpin the track and provide the central [[Harmonic|harmonic component]], particularly since there is no bass to speak of aside from a pitched bass drum sample". Regarding Ricch's craft as a writer, Mall noted "the fact that he retains writing credit here and on several other tracks that are charting, including those where he is a featured artist, speaks to a strong business savvy on his part".<ref name="Time Viral">{{Cite magazine|last=Lang|first=Cady|date=February 18, 2020|title=Going Viral Helped Catapult Roddy Ricch and 'The Box' to #1 — But There's More to the Story|url=https://time.com/5784337/roddy-ricch-the-box-interview/|access-date=March 25, 2020|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}}</ref>

''[[Vulture magazine|Vulture]]''{{'}}s Paul Thompson said Ricch "raps with verve", calling the song "strange and eccentric", while noting Ricch's vocal versatility in the song, writing, he "moves easily between vocal modes, sounding defiant ('I won't ever sell my ''soooooouuuuuullllll'', and I can back that<nowiki/>'), conspiratorial ('<nowiki/>'Got a bitch that's looking like [[Aaliyah]] — she a model'<nowiki/>'), or playful — like when he cackles unnervingly at the beginning of the second verse".<ref name="Vulture">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2020/01/roddy-ricch-the-box-explained.html|title=How Roddy Ricch's 'The Box' Just Became Rap's First Viral No. 1 Hit of 2020|last=Thompson|first=Paul|date=January 13, 2020|website=[[New York (magazine)#Digital|Vulture]]|access-date=February 16, 2020}}</ref> The song's title has been noted as being a possible reference to jail ("[[Solitary confinement|the box]]" being a slang term for "jail").,<ref name="OCC" /> "The Box" is played in the [[tempo]] of 117 [[Beats per minute|BPM]] and [[key signature]] of [[B-flat minor|B♭ minor]] with a [[time signature]] of 4/4 in common time.
sections.text:
"The Box" was the last song Ricch made for Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial. It was recorded in roughly 15 minutes in the early morning hours in New York after Ricch had been recording all night. The song begins with a "triumphant introduction that amounts to an orchestral swell", which many listeners attributed to as a sample of the intro on "Love Sex Magic" by Ciara. However, the song's producer, 30 Roc, has insisted that though similar, the "swell" is not a sample of "Love Sex Magic", explaining: "It is not a sample. It's really a VST [plug-in] using Omnisphere [production software]." Ricch said he decided to place "The Box" as track two on the album, because "it just bangs [and] the 808s hit so hard".

The song's intro contains a "squeaky sound", known as the "eee err" sound, which is also heard throughout the rest of the song. According to Atlantic Records A&R Keefa Black, after the song was finished, Ricch said "Wait let me add something", and came up with the sound himself. Speaking on where the inspiration for the sound came from, he said "I seen Michael Jackson do it...That's what made me want to do it. Cause he was in the studio one time and he was talking about some song that he made but he started beatboxing and he said he put that in the beat". The squeaky sound has inspired many memes online. Musicologist and Northeastern University  professor of music Andrew Mall said the "eee err" sound is not exactly the most interesting component of the song's beat, instead pointing out Ricch's skill as a songwriter: "I'm really taken by the atmospheric synths that underpin the track and provide the central harmonic component, particularly since there is no bass to speak of aside from a pitched bass drum sample". Regarding Ricch's craft as a writer, Mall noted "the fact that he retains writing credit here and on several other tracks that are charting, including those where he is a featured artist, speaks to a strong business savvy on his part".

Vulture{{'}}s Paul Thompson said Ricch "raps with verve", calling the song "strange and eccentric", while noting Ricch's vocal versatility in the song, writing, he "moves easily between vocal modes, sounding defiant ('I won't ever sell my soooooouuuuuullllll, and I can back that<nowiki/>'), conspiratorial ('<nowiki/>'Got a bitch that's looking like Aaliyah — she a model'<nowiki/>'), or playful — like when he cackles unnervingly at the beginning of the second verse". The song's title has been noted as being a possible reference to jail ("the box" being a slang term for "jail")., "The Box" is played in the tempo of 117 BPM and key signature of B♭ minor with a time signature of 4/4 in common time.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
The song was acclaimed by music critics. Along with the tracks "Boom Boom Room" and "[[Start wit Me]]" featuring [[Gunna (rapper)|Gunna]], Darryl Robertson of ''[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]'' felt that "The Box" is "further proof that the Atlantic Records-signee can pen addictive radio-friendly records".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vibe.com/2019/12/roddy-ricc-antisocial-tour|title=Roddy Ricch Kicks Off His 'Antisocial Tour' By Selling Out L.A.'s Hollywood Palladium|work=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]|last=Robertson|first=Darryl|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref> Josh Svetz of ''[[HipHopDX]]'' echoed a similar sentiment, writing that "The appeal to Roddy is simple; the kid can write a hell of a hook. Whether it's the head-bopping harmony on 'The Box' or the flute backed, Gunna-assisted single, 'Start Wit Me,' Roddy excels at producing choruses that stick and only get better with repeat listens."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hiphopdx.com/reviews/id.3590/title.review-roddy-ricch-justifies-the-hype-on-please-excuse-me-for-being-antisocial|title=Review: Roddy Ricch Justifies The Hype On 'Please Excuse Me For Being Antisocial'|work=[[HipHopDX]]|last=Svetz|first=Josh|date=December 26, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'', Alphonse Pierre stated that on the song, which features a "hard-hitting beat that sounds like a teapot is boiling in the background, [Ricch] finds a new delivery and pitch nearly every 10 seconds. The track is the best example of Roddy's versatility, which has been both a blessing and a curse."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/roddy-ricch-please-excuse-me-for-being-antisocial/|title=Roddy Ricch: Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial Review|website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|last=Pierre|first=Alphonse|date=December 12, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref>

Praising the song, ''HotNewHipHop''{{'}}s Mitch Findlay asserted that although its [[Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial|parent album]] "yielded plenty of highlights, none stood out quite so much as 'The Box'". Findlay called the song's "eee err" intro "creative and soon-to-be-iconic" and labeled Ricch's flow as confident and charismatic.<ref name="HNHH">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/233486-roddy-ricch-celebrates-the-box-being-the-worlds-1-song-news|title=Roddy Ricch Celebrates "The Box" Being The World's #1 Song|website=HotNewHipHop|last=Findlay|first=Mitch|date=January 2, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}}</ref> Heran Mamo of ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' opined that Ricch "comes armed and ready with his verses despite the rather lighthearted 'hee-hoo' ad-libs in the background". Mamo noted that in the song, Ricch raps about acquiring and protecting "his necessary riches".<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/lyrics/8546850/roddy-ricch-the-box-lyrics|title=Here Are the Lyrics to Roddy Ricch's 'The Box'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|last=Mamo|first=Heran|date=December 19, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was acclaimed by music critics. Along with the tracks "Boom Boom Room" and "Start wit Me" featuring Gunna, Darryl Robertson of Vibe felt that "The Box" is "further proof that the Atlantic Records-signee can pen addictive radio-friendly records". Josh Svetz of HipHopDX echoed a similar sentiment, writing that "The appeal to Roddy is simple; the kid can write a hell of a hook. Whether it's the head-bopping harmony on 'The Box' or the flute backed, Gunna-assisted single, 'Start Wit Me,' Roddy excels at producing choruses that stick and only get better with repeat listens." Writing for Pitchfork, Alphonse Pierre stated that on the song, which features a "hard-hitting beat that sounds like a teapot is boiling in the background, [Ricch] finds a new delivery and pitch nearly every 10 seconds. The track is the best example of Roddy's versatility, which has been both a blessing and a curse."

Praising the song, HotNewHipHop{{'}}s Mitch Findlay asserted that although its parent album "yielded plenty of highlights, none stood out quite so much as 'The Box'". Findlay called the song's "eee err" intro "creative and soon-to-be-iconic" and labeled Ricch's flow as confident and charismatic. Heran Mamo of Billboard opined that Ricch "comes armed and ready with his verses despite the rather lighthearted 'hee-hoo' ad-libs in the background". Mamo noted that in the song, Ricch raps about acquiring and protecting "his necessary riches".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "The Box" spent eleven weeks at the top spot of the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]],<ref name="Trust">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9340653/roddy-ricch-the-box-harry-styles-adore-you-hot-100|title=Roddy Ricch's 'The Box' Leads Hot 100 for 11th Week, Harry Styles' 'Adore You' Hits Top 10|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=March 23, 2020|access-date=March 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9346375/weeknd-blinding-lights-number-one-hot-100|title=The Weeknd's 'Blinding Lights' Hits No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100, Doja Cat's 'Say So' Enters Top 10|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=March 30, 2020|access-date=March 30, 2020}}</ref> after debuting at number 47 on the issue dated December 21, 2019, and reaching number one four weeks later, becoming Ricch's first number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 as well as the first new song to top the chart in the 2020s decade—since both "[[All I Want for Christmas Is You]]" by [[Mariah Carey]] and "[[Circles (Post Malone song)|Circles]]" by [[Post Malone]] began their runs at the top position in 2019. During the same week, the song logged its second week at number one on ''Billboard''{{'}}s [[Streaming Songs]] chart (drawing 68.2 million streams) and jumped to number eight on the [[Digital Songs]] chart as well, with 11,000 downloads sold. Additionally, the song reached the top spot on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] and [[Hot Rap Songs]] charts as well, becoming Ricch's first number-one song on both charts.<ref name="Hot 100">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/8547900/roddy-ricch-the-box-hot-100-number-one|title=Roddy Ricch's 'The Box' Bounds to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100, Justin Bieber's 'Yummy' Debuts at No. 2|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=January 13, 2020|access-date=January 14, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Trust"/>
sections.text: "The Box" spent eleven weeks at the top spot of the US Billboard Hot 100, after debuting at number 47 on the issue dated December 21, 2019, and reaching number one four weeks later, becoming Ricch's first number one on the Billboard Hot 100 as well as the first new song to top the chart in the 2020s decade—since both "All I Want for Christmas Is You" by Mariah Carey and "Circles" by Post Malone began their runs at the top position in 2019. During the same week, the song logged its second week at number one on Billboard{{'}}s Streaming Songs chart (drawing 68.2 million streams) and jumped to number eight on the Digital Songs chart as well, with 11,000 downloads sold. Additionally, the song reached the top spot on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and Hot Rap Songs charts as well, becoming Ricch's first number-one song on both charts.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The song's audio video was released on December 6, 2019, in conjunction with the album,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uLHqpjW3aDs|title=Roddy Ricch - The Box [Official Audio]|date=5 December 2019 |via=[[YouTube]]|access-date=July 1, 2020}}</ref> accumulating 454 million views on YouTube as of February 2026.

The song's official music video premiered on [[YouTube]] on February 28, 2020, and has over 765 million views as of April 2026. It was directed by Ricch, with co-direction by [[Christian Breslauer]], who also directed Ricch's previous two music videos, for "Boom Boom Room" and "[[Tip Toe (Roddy Ricch song)|Tip Toe]]".<ref name="EW Video">{{Cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/music/roddy-ricch-finally-drops-the-box-music-video/|title=Roddy Ricch finally drops 'The Box' music video after seven weeks atop the charts|last=Jones|first=Marcus|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly|EW.com]]|date=February 28, 2020|access-date=March 21, 2020}}</ref><ref name="MTV Video">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mtv.ca/roddy-ricch-the-box-video/|title=Roddy Ricch Dunks, Races, And Dances In His Long-Awaited Video For 'The Box'|last=Roth|first=Madeline|date=February 28, 2020|website=[[MTV News|MTV Canada]]|access-date=March 10, 2020}}</ref> Ricch explained via [[Twitter]] the reason why the video took a "lil time" to be released was because he directed it.<ref>{{Cite tweet|url=https://twitter.com/RoddyRicch/status/1233606444936658944|title=it took me a lil time cause i directed it but the box music video out now...|number=1233606444936658944|user=RoddyRicch|author=Roddy Ricch|date=February 28, 2020|accessdate=March 10, 2020}}</ref>

[[File:Roddy Ricch - The Box (music video screenshot).png|thumb|Ricch inside a glass box in a museum.]]
The "action-packed"<ref name="MTV Video" /><ref name="XXL Video">{{Cite web|url=https://www.xxlmag.com/news/2020/02/roddy-ricch-the-box-video/|title=Roddy Ricch Drops "The Box" video: Watch|work=[[XXL Magazine|XXL]]|last=Fitzgerald|first=Trent|date=February 28, 2020|access-date=March 21, 2020}}</ref> video starts with Ricch speeding in a "super charged" [[muscle car]]<ref name="XXL Video" /> in a "''[[Fast & Furious]]''-style [[Street racing|street race]]".<ref name="MTV Video" /> During the race, Ricch turns on his [[turbocharger|turbos]] and "outdrives his opponent who eventually crashes and burns, leaving Ricch the victor of the contest".<ref name="XXL Video" /> The video then cuts to a basketball game, where Ricch is seen scoring the game-winning shot, "flying" in the air, akin to NBA icon [[Michael Jordan]],<ref name="XXL Video" /> with what [[MTV News|MTV]]'s Madeline Roth called an "impressive (and definitely far-fetched)" [[slam dunk]].<ref name="MTV Video" /> Ricch is then seen carrying out a major [[bank heist]].<ref name="XXL Video" /> Multiple scenes reference the song's lyrics, such as when Ricch delivers a speech from the [[White House]],<ref name="MTV Video" /> alluding to the line "I'm a 2020 president candidate". Halle Kiefer of [[New York (magazine)#Digital expansion and destination sites|Vulture]] noted a theme in the video: "the visual follows Ricch's unstoppable success as it takes him to surreal lengths, whether it be lounging on a bed suspended over sharks, casually walking up the side of a building or dancing in front of an explosive game of chicken".<ref name="Vulture Video">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2020/02/rapper-roddy-ricch-releases-the-box-music-video-watch.html|title=Roddy Ricch Is the One to Beat in His New 'The Box' Music Video|last=Kiefer|first=Halle|date=February 28, 2020|website=[[New York (magazine)#Digital expansion and destination sites|Vulture]]|access-date=March 10, 2020}}</ref> The video concludes with Ricch inside a glass box, "preserved for future generations inside a museum exhibit".<ref name="Vulture Video" />
sections.text:
thumb|Ricch inside a glass box in a museum.
The "action-packed" video starts with Ricch speeding in a "super charged" muscle car in a "Fast & Furious-style street race". During the race, Ricch turns on his turbos and "outdrives his opponent who eventually crashes and burns, leaving Ricch the victor of the contest". The video then cuts to a basketball game, where Ricch is seen scoring the game-winning shot, "flying" in the air, akin to NBA icon Michael Jordan, with what MTV's Madeline Roth called an "impressive (and definitely far-fetched)" slam dunk. Ricch is then seen carrying out a major bank heist. Multiple scenes reference the song's lyrics, such as when Ricch delivers a speech from the White House, alluding to the line "I'm a 2020 president candidate". Halle Kiefer of Vulture noted a theme in the video: "the visual follows Ricch's unstoppable success as it takes him to surreal lengths, whether it be lounging on a bed suspended over sharks, casually walking up the side of a building or dancing in front of an explosive game of chicken". The video concludes with Ricch inside a glass box, "preserved for future generations inside a museum exhibit".
